sense: one who finds fault with a person or a plan

terms.gloss: a critic, one who finds fault
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.7: restat ūnum genus reprehēnsōrum
terms.comment: From reprehendere, to find fault with: the critic of a person, a decision or a book.

evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.31: obtrectātōrēs autem et invidī Scīpiōnis
terms.comment: Stronger than reprehēnsor: one who runs another down, often from envy or rivalry, as its pairing with invidī shows.

phrases.latin: Restat ūnum genus reprehēnsōrum, quibus Acadēmīae ratiō nōn probātur.
phrases.english: There remains one kind of critic: those who do not approve of the Academy’s method.

sources: Lewis & Short: reprehensor · Lewis & Short: obtrectator
